Equipment and measurement:
The provider delivers and installs meters, sensors and related hardware, then tracks use by suite, common area or system.
Operations and maintenance:
The provider monitors performance, handles repairs and replacements, and keeps data flowing.

The provider issues charges and reports that show who used what, and whether the building is improving.
Think of a managed fleet. You get the vehicle, the upkeep and the reporting. You don't own the parts and you don't carry the repair risk.

Expect several weeks from agreement to live meters. Equipment lead time drives most of that schedule, and panel condition, permits and suite access can each push the date. Get the lead time confirmed in writing before you sign.

may change at any time in accordance with applicable laws

and saved approximately

Pull baseline bills
from the last 12 months, by commodity.
Estimate the recoverable share
after removing common-area load.
Total the fee load

Calculate the net change to NOI
under low, expected and high occupancy.

children.text: Benchmarking Turns Data Into Decisions
Benchmarking means comparing your building with similar buildings, its own historical use, or reference performance levels.
Natural Resources Canada's national building energy benchmarking initiative
describes ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager benchmarks covering
more than 80 building types
using weather data from
over 150 Canadian stations
. Use that kind of weather-normalised comparison, or you'll chase winter spikes that aren't faults.

The control loop is practical. Submeters feed suite, common-area, water and thermal data to us. We aggregate and normalise it. You compare against history and peers, and anomalies trigger maintenance. Owners and residents can access consumption data, so a dispute starts with a shared record instead of an opinion.
Leaks Need More Than a Water Meter
We include leak and flood detection, own and maintain all leak detection equipment, and include sensor batteries, replacements and system updates. Don't oversell water metering alone.
A water submeter alone does not detect every possible leak.
Consumption data reveals unusual usage patterns, dedicated sensors detect water at selected locations, and a combined design provides broader protection than either alone.
Watch three signals every month:
Unusual overnight water use:
Points to leaks, running toilets or failed valves.
Creep in common-area load:
Points to stuck equipment, lighting schedules or heating faults.
Suites far above peers:
Points to behaviour, faulty appliances or a meter problem to verify.
Act on those signals within one billing cycle. Data you ignore has no operational value.
Tenant Costs and Affordability Protections

Move a flat, rent-inclusive utility into a submetered bill and NOI improves in month one. The tenant sees a new charge with no explanation. That is how a cost-control project becomes an arrears file. Energy as a service changes who carries cost, risk and tenant friction, not only how much energy the building uses. Test the model against two documents: your own baseline bills and the tenant's proposed bill.
Canada's 2025-2026 Energy Fact Book reports households spent an average of
$2,376 on in-home energy in 2023
, equal to
3% of disposable income
, while
5.6% spent at least 10% of income on energy
. That average hides harder cases in low-income, electrically heated, older or poorly insulated suites. A new service fee can push a household into arrears even when total building consumption falls.

Make this a launch condition: an annual written summary of consumption, charges, commodity costs, fees, and the conditions under which fees can increase. Plain language, before launch, not after the first complaint. Ask any provider for it. If yours cannot produce it, that tells you what tenant support will look like.

Every tenant should get clear answers to three questions. Who keeps the savings when consumption falls? How do escalation clauses change the administration fee over time? Can I verify my own reading against my bill? If your leasing team stumbles on those, the communications are not ready. Neither is the contract.

Separate lower consumption from cost reallocation in your reporting. Billing tenants for what you used to absorb improves NOI, but it is not an energy saving. Report both numbers. Owners who blur them lose the argument the first time a tenant asks why the bill went up while the building "saved energy."

A single invoice for electricity, gas, water and thermal charges is convenient. It also concentrates payment risk. Under Axis Meter's terms, a partial payment on a single invoice is applied first to electricity submetering services. Axis Meter then decides at its sole discretion how to apply the balance to water, gas or thermal energy services. Know that order before you promise tenants a simple bill.
Non-Payment Rules Are Ontario-Specific Here
For Ontario electricity, Axis Meter may
disconnect, terminate, or limit electricity delivery

for unpaid electricity or electricity-related charges after lawful demand and notice, until charges are paid in full. Axis Meter's security deposit policy for electricity submetering services in Ontario is consistent with Ontario Energy Board requirements. Those disconnection, deposit and payment-allocation rules apply to Ontario electricity submetering. Water, gas and projects outside Ontario are reviewed separately for each jurisdiction, so verify local rules before you adopt the same terms.
Request these protections in writing:
Plain-language fee schedule:
Every recurring and one-time charge, with escalation terms.
Reading access:
Resident access to their own consumption data.
Hardship process:
Notice steps, payment plan route and dispute contact before disconnection.
Rent treatment:
How any rent adjustment interacts with new utility charges under local law.
Don't sign a deal that improves your statement by making the tenant's bill unaffordable. Arrears, turnover and vacancies will take the gain back.
Choosing Metering for Two-Way and Demand-Response Buildings

A building with solar, batteries, heat pumps or demand response isn't a standard submetering job. Energy flows both ways, timing matters, and a meter that only totals monthly consumption can't value exports, storage or peak reduction fairly.

Does not capture generation or storage exports

Mixed-use buildings with solar, heat pumps and submetering

Demand Response Needs Controllable, Measured Loads

Demand response works when granular data identifies controllable HVAC, domestic hot-water and pumping loads, then automated controls reduce demand during qualifying events. Program value depends on eligibility, baselines and verification, so preserve interval records and document override and comfort limits in advance. Review the programme structures in our guide to
demand response programs
and confirm eligibility before counting any revenue.
The data architecture is essential. You need interval records of
imports and exports with timestamps

, separated into common-area, suite, storage and generation flows. Without that separation, we could allocate consumption but couldn't fairly credit shared solar generation, battery charging or peak reduction.
Ontario has formalised export data handling. Our overview of
smart meters in Ontario
notes amendments gave the Smart Metering Entity authority to collect and manage behind-the-meter generation and storage export data, with exclusive authority over smart-metering data effective
January 1, 2025
. Confirm who holds that responsibility in your project.

Settle these before installation:
Data ownership:
Who owns interval data and who can export it at term end.
Settlement and credits:
How resident bill credits for generation or load reduction are calculated.
Degradation and backup:
Who pays as batteries degrade and what loads stay live in an outage.
Regulatory responsibility:
Who files, reports and answers the regulator.
Our Ontario licence covers electricity submetering in Ontario only, and water, gas and projects outside Ontario are reviewed separately for each jurisdiction. Build that review into your schedule.
Confirm the Contract Terms Before You Sign
Don't sign on a savings estimate. Sign on verified credentials, a complete fee schedule and a baseline you supplied.
Use this checklist:
Verify the licence:
Axis Meter Solutions Inc. is licensed by the Ontario Energy Board as a unit sub-meter provider for electricity unit sub-metering services in Ontario under
licence ES-2022-0268
, which can be verified on the Ontario Energy Board register. That licence covers Ontario electricity only.
Confirm commodities:
State whether electricity, gas, water and thermal energy are each included.
Request the fee schedule:
Service Fees are the administration fee and other charges and fees for our Services. Get how each can change.
Check term and exit:
Confirm term length, buyout, meter replacement and end-of-term data return.
Confirm rate language:
Charges are based on rates that may change at any time in accordance with applicable laws.
Test resident handling:
Ask how billing, move-in, move-out and disputes are handled, and compare the model with an
energy service company
structure if ownership matters to you.

Take one concrete step this month. Request a site assessment for one building, then compare the quote against 12 months of baseline bills using the NOI test. If the net result is clear under conservative occupancy, proceed. If it isn't, don't.

We provide turnkey energy as a service through provider-owned submetering for electricity, water, gas and thermal loads, including assessment, installation, commissioning, resident billing, leak detection and ongoing monitoring with $0 upfront under our standard model. Request a site assessment for one building, bring 12 months of baseline bills, and we'll model recoverable costs and fees against your current NOI before you commit. Visit

Energy as a service changes who carries cost, risk and tenant friction, not only how much energy the building uses. Test the model against two documents: your own baseline bills and the tenant's proposed bill.

Canada's 2025-2026 Energy Fact Book reports households spent an average of $2,376 on in-home energy in 2023, equal to 3% of disposable income, while 5.6% spent at least 10% of income on energy. That average hides harder cases in low-income, electrically heated, older or poorly insulated suites. A new service fee can push a household into arrears even when total building consumption falls.

Transparency Tenants Can Actually Use

Make this a launch condition: an annual written summary of consumption, charges, commodity costs, fees, and the conditions under which fees can increase. Plain language, before launch, not after the first complaint. Ask any provider for it. If yours cannot produce it, that tells you what tenant support will look like.

Every tenant should get clear answers to three questions. Who keeps the savings when consumption falls? How do escalation clauses change the administration fee over time? Can I verify my own reading against my bill? If your leasing team stumbles on those, the communications are not ready. Neither is the contract.

Separate lower consumption from cost reallocation in your reporting. Billing tenants for what you used to absorb improves NOI, but it is not an energy saving. Report both numbers. Owners who blur them lose the argument the first time a tenant asks why the bill went up while the building "saved energy."

A single invoice for electricity, gas, water and thermal charges is convenient. It also concentrates payment risk. Under Axis Meter's terms, a partial payment on a single invoice is applied first to electricity submetering services. Axis Meter then decides at its sole discretion how to apply the balance to water, gas or thermal energy services. Know that order before you promise tenants a simple bill.

Non-Payment Rules Are Ontario-Specific Here

For Ontario electricity, Axis Meter may disconnect, terminate, or limit electricity delivery for unpaid electricity or electricity-related charges after lawful demand and notice, until charges are paid in full. Axis Meter's security deposit policy for electricity submetering services in Ontario is consistent with Ontario Energy Board requirements. Those disconnection, deposit and payment-allocation rules apply to Ontario electricity submetering. Water, gas and projects outside Ontario are reviewed separately for each jurisdiction, so verify local rules before you adopt the same terms.

Request these protections in writing:

  • Plain-language fee schedule: Every recurring and one-time charge, with escalation terms.
  • Reading access: Resident access to their own consumption data.
  • Hardship process: Notice steps, payment plan route and dispute contact before disconnection.
  • Rent treatment: How any rent adjustment interacts with new utility charges under local law.

Don't sign a deal that improves your statement by making the tenant's bill unaffordable. Arrears, turnover and vacancies will take the gain back.

Choosing Metering for Two-Way and Demand-Response Buildings

A building with solar, batteries, heat pumps or demand response isn't a standard submetering job. Energy flows both ways, timing matters, and a meter that only totals monthly consumption can't value exports, storage or peak reduction fairly.

Approach Best fit Data captured Main limitation
Conventional suite submetering Multi-family buildings billed on consumption Consumption per suite Does not capture generation or storage exports
Whole-building measurement Owners who need building-level performance Total building load Cannot allocate costs to individual suites alone
Bidirectional metering Buildings with solar or battery storage Imports and exports with timestamps Needs clear rules for crediting and settlement
Hybrid system Mixed-use buildings with solar, heat pumps and submetering Suite, common-area and generation flows Highest data and contract complexity

Demand Response Needs Controllable, Measured Loads

Demand response works when granular data identifies controllable HVAC, domestic hot-water and pumping loads, then automated controls reduce demand during qualifying events. Program value depends on eligibility, baselines and verification, so preserve interval records and document override and comfort limits in advance. Review the programme structures in our guide to demand response programs and confirm eligibility before counting any revenue.

The data architecture is essential. You need interval records of imports and exports with timestamps, separated into common-area, suite, storage and generation flows. Without that separation, we could allocate consumption but couldn't fairly credit shared solar generation, battery charging or peak reduction.

Ontario has formalised export data handling. Our overview of smart meters in Ontario notes amendments gave the Smart Metering Entity authority to collect and manage behind-the-meter generation and storage export data, with exclusive authority over smart-metering data effective January 1, 2025. Confirm who holds that responsibility in your project.

Contract Issues the Table Cannot Show

Settle these before installation:

  • Data ownership: Who owns interval data and who can export it at term end.
  • Settlement and credits: How resident bill credits for generation or load reduction are calculated.
  • Degradation and backup: Who pays as batteries degrade and what loads stay live in an outage.
  • Regulatory responsibility: Who files, reports and answers the regulator.

Our Ontario licence covers electricity submetering in Ontario only, and water, gas and projects outside Ontario are reviewed separately for each jurisdiction. Build that review into your schedule.

Confirm the Contract Terms Before You Sign

Don't sign on a savings estimate. Sign on verified credentials, a complete fee schedule and a baseline you supplied.

Use this checklist:

  • Verify the licence: Axis Meter Solutions Inc. is licensed by the Ontario Energy Board as a unit sub-meter provider for electricity unit sub-metering services in Ontario under licence ES-2022-0268, which can be verified on the Ontario Energy Board register. That licence covers Ontario electricity only.
  • Confirm commodities: State whether electricity, gas, water and thermal energy are each included.
  • Request the fee schedule: Service Fees are the administration fee and other charges and fees for our Services. Get how each can change.
  • Check term and exit: Confirm term length, buyout, meter replacement and end-of-term data return.
  • Confirm rate language: Charges are based on rates that may change at any time in accordance with applicable laws.
  • Test resident handling: Ask how billing, move-in, move-out and disputes are handled, and compare the model with an energy service company structure if ownership matters to you.

Take one concrete step this month. Request a site assessment for one building, then compare the quote against 12 months of baseline bills using the NOI test. If the net result is clear under conservative occupancy, proceed. If it isn't, don't.
